$comment: Neutral shipped <sys/types.h> (POSIX) — the base system typedefs, as language-NEUTRAL aliases injected by the semantic phase (see README + stdint.json). FIRST shipped descriptor in a SUBDIRECTORY: `#include <sys/types.h>` maps to `sys/types.json` (resolveSystemDescriptor preserves the subdir), DISTINCT from a top-level `<time.h>` -> `time.json` (so the later `<sys/time.h>` -> `sys/time.json` cannot collide). Widths are the LP64 model shared by the runnable unix targets (linux x86-64 + arm64): off_t/ssize_t/blksize_t/blkcnt_t/suseconds_t = the C `long` (i64); dev_t/ino_t/nlink_t = unsigned long (u64); mode_t/uid_t/gid_t/id_t/useconds_t = unsigned int (u32); pid_t/key_t = int (i32). These are the EXACT glibc x86-64 + arm64 (LP64, identical) widths the `struct stat`/`struct flock`/`struct timeval` layouts (later cycles) depend on, and they are the RUN-GREEN target (linux). macOS differs for several (mode_t = u16, dev_t = i32, nlink_t = u16, blksize_t = i32; off_t/ssize_t/uid_t/gid_t/pid_t/ino_t agree) — a descriptor baking a single platform's widths, deferred D-LANG-PLATFORM-DEPENDENT-PRIMITIVE-WIDTH (the same class as the stdint/stddef ILP32 deferral). It is INERT for the self-contained `shipped_sys_types` corpus (scalar `mode_t = 0` etc. — the width never affects the result); it FIRST bites at the FFI boundary (the macOS `struct stat` field layout, a later cycle), where a per-target width resolution closes it. time_t IS re-provided here with per-dataModel spelling arms (long on LP64, long long on LLP64) BYTE-identical to <time.h>'s time_t — the F_ShippedTypeIdentityConflict consistency check (D-LANG-TYPE-IDENTITY-VOCABULARY) enforces that every descriptor declaring a shared typedef resolves it identically per target ( the first-wins `injectedNames` dedup makes the multi-header provision benign — a TU including both silently takes the first-read) because sqlite test_quota.c reaches time_t THROUGH <sys/types.h> and would otherwise fail; clock_t stays owned by <time.h> alone. ★ D-LANG-TYPE-IDENTITY-VOCABULARY (2026-07-20): a vocabulary TAG (`i64 "long"`) names a C type whose WIDTH is a property of the DATA MODEL, so a FLAT tag is only legal on a descriptor whose formats all share one model. This file ships on elf+macho (LP64) AND pe (LLP64), so `ssize_t` gained per-format arms exactly like its `off_t` sibling: LP64 spells it `long` (glibc/Darwin `__ssize_t`), while on LLP64 `long` is 32-BIT and the 64-bit signed size type is `long long` (MSVC's `SSIZE_T` is `__int64`). A flat `i64 "long"` here was a PHANTOM on pe — the pair (I64,"long") is unproducible under LLP64, so `_Generic(aSsizeT, long long:, long:)` matched NEITHER arm and `long long *p = aSsizeTPtr;` failed S0003. The invariant — a tag must have the width the LANGUAGE gives that name under the SELECTED data model — is now MACHINE-CHECKED by `checkShippedTypeConsistency` / tests/ffi/test_shipped_type_consistency.cpp, which enumerates every descriptor across every shipped target. No `library` (typedefs have no link surface); no `symbols`/`constants`/`macros`. ★★ TF-C90 / D-CSUBSET-SYS-TYPES-BSD-SPELLING-GROUP-ABSENT — THE BSD-COMPAT SPELLING GROUP (`u_char` `u_short` `u_int` `u_long` `quad_t` `u_quad_t` `caddr_t` `fixpt_t` `segsz_t`), the family every unix `<sys/types.h>` ships together and the WINDOWS one ships NOT AT ALL. Every one carries `variants` and NO flat `type`, because PER-ENTRY AVAILABILITY IS EXPRESSED BY WHICH `variants` EXIST — the same mechanism `off64_t` above already uses to be elf-only (shipped_lib_descriptor.cpp: 0 matching variants ⇒ `selected == false` ⇒ the typedef is NOT injected). That keeps the descriptor honest per-platform with NO identity branch in the engine, and it is why `availableObjectFormats` stays [elf,macho,pe]: the HEADER is available everywhere, these NAMES are not. ✔MEASURED per-name against three reference header sets on the build host rather than asserted — musl (emsdk sysroot `sys/types.h:63-69`) declares u_char/u_short/u_int/u_long/quad_t/u_quad_t/caddr_t; bionic (Android NDK sysroot `sys/types.h:54,136-139`) declares u_char/u_short/u_int/u_long/caddr_t; mingw-w64 x86_64 `sys/types.h` declares NONE of the nine; the macOS SDK `sys/types.h:84-128` declares all nine. So the first seven are elf+macho and `fixpt_t`/`segsz_t` are BSD-ONLY, absent from BOTH linux libcs, hence macho-only here. ★ WHY THIS GROUP IS REACHED AT ALL, because it is not what a reader expects: the sqlite corpus never SPELLS these names (`grep -rnw` over src/ ext/ bld-dss/ finds zero). They are spelled by REAL macOS SDK HEADERS that DSS reads through the angle-include SOURCE FALLBACK (D-INCLUDE-ANGLE-SOURCE-FALLBACK) because those headers ship no descriptor — `<sys/sysctl.h>`'s `struct extern_proc` (`caddr_t user_stack`, `fixpt_t p_pctcpu`, `u_quad_t p_uticks`, `segsz_t e_xsize`) and `int sysctl(int *, u_int, …)`. Their own `#include <sys/types.h>` is intercepted at priority 1 by THIS descriptor (include_path_resolve.hpp: descriptor first; a real source header only on a descriptor MISS), so a name this file omits can NEVER be declared no matter what the platform header holds. ★ SPELLING TAGS, and the asymmetry is deliberate: `u_long` is tagged `unsigned long` because all four reference headers spell it exactly that and the typedef name IS that spelling. `quad_t`/`u_quad_t` are UNTAGGED (the dev_t/ino_t/blkcnt_t form) because the reference platforms DISAGREE on the spelling — glibc's `__quad_t` is `long int` on 64-bit while musl and Darwin (int64_t/u_int64_t) spell it `long long` — and there is no measured consumer of the SPELLING, only of the 64-bit width; inventing one arm would be the PHANTOM-TAG mistake D-LANG-TYPE-IDENTITY-VOCABULARY records for ssize_t, and the width divergence stays under D-LANG-PLATFORM-DEPENDENT-PRIMITIVE-WIDTH with the rest of this file. ✔MEASURED that an UNTAGGED u8/u16/u32 IS the language's `unsigned char`/`unsigned short`/`unsigned int` (a `_Generic` probe over uint8_t/uint16_t/uint32_t/mode_t matches every arm, and `u64 "unsigned long"` matches `unsigned long`), so u_char/u_short/u_int/fixpt_t/segsz_t need no tag to BE the right C types. ⚠ WHAT THIS ROW IS *NOT*: the macho `S0006` residual left after this group is `__uint128_t` (D-CSUBSET-UINT128-TYPE, ✔MEASURED x9 = src/util.c 5 + src/mem1.c 2 + src/test1.c 2) and `__builtin_va_list` (D-CSUBSET-BUILTIN-VA-LIST-TYPE-NAME, x2, from the SDK's `<sys/_types/_va_list.h>` `typedef __builtin_va_list __darwin_va_list;`). Both are COMPILER-PROVIDED TYPE NAMES, not header typedefs — no descriptor can supply them and NOTHING in this file addresses them. Adding either name here would be wrong.
